issues.description: _enable_vad invariant uses end_of_utterance_mode but the user-facing default is turn_detection_mode
issues.detail: The default is changed to TurnDetectionMode.FIXED, and the changelog states VAD/interruption frames are only emitted when the mode is not FIXED/EXTERNAL. But the actual gate at line ~334 reads from self._config.end_of_utterance_mode (EndOfUtteranceMode), not params.turn_detection_mode. The invariant 'enable_vad iff user did not pick a Pipecat-controlled mode' is not stated, and the reader cannot verify without tracing how turn_detection_mode maps onto end_of_utterance_mode. State the invariant in a comment and/or derive _enable_vad directly from turn_detection_mode so the two stay in lockstep.

issues.description: Frame-handling branch loses behavior for non-VAD UserStoppedSpeakingFrame without a stated rationale
issues.detail: Previously, isinstance(frame, UserStoppedSpeakingFrame) triggered finalize() when VAD was disabled. The patch narrows the trigger to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame only. If VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is a subclass of UserStoppedSpeakingFrame this is a strict tightening of acceptance; if not, any pipeline that emits a plain UserStoppedSpeakingFrame (e.g., manual/programmatic stops) will silently stop finalizing the transcript. The change deserves an explicit comment stating the class hierarchy assumption and the intended invariant ('finalize only on VAD-originated stop frames'), and ideally a test covering both frame types.

issues.description: split_sentences default is silently coerced; SpeechSegmentConfig is always overwritten
issues.detail: params.split_sentences is typed Optional[bool] (default None), but _prepare_config also lists it in the generic copy loop AND then unconditionally sets config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False). The unconditional assignment overwrites any speech_segment_config that an earlier branch may have set and conflates None with False. State explicitly that None means 'off', and either skip the generic-copy entry for split_sentences or skip the explicit assignment - not both. Pick one channel for this parameter so the reader does not have to reason about which write wins.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics() call moved without explanation
issues.detail: The dead-comment '# await self.start_processing_metrics()' is relocated from after to before the broadcast/interrupt calls. Commented-out code with no rationale is exactly the kind of artifact a literate reader stumbles over. Either delete it or add a one-line comment explaining why it's parked there and under what condition it should be reenabled.

issues.description: Changelog files disagree on what was added vs fixed
issues.detail: changelog/3328.added.md mentions only split_sentences; changelog/3328.fixed.md covers the VAD frame change, the default change to FIXED, and the conditional VAD-frame emission. The new FIXED enum value itself is arguably an 'added' item, not 'fixed.' Minor, but a careful reader of the release notes will be unable to tell whether FIXED is a new API surface or just a default change.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The diff is small and the intent is reasonable, but the central invariant - 'VAD frames are emitted iff the user chose a non-Pipecat-controlled turn-detection mode' - is never stated in code, and the gate is implemented against end_of_utterance_mode while the user-facing knob is turn_detection_mode. The frame-handler change from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is a behavioral narrowing whose correctness depends on a class-hierarchy assumption the reader has to take on faith. split_sentences is written through two channels (generic copy loop + unconditional SpeechSegmentConfig overwrite), which is the kind of double-write a literate-programming pass would catch. None of these are algorithmically deep - there is no hot path, no complexity claim to audit - but the readability and stated-invariant bar is below what foundational service code deserves. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the VAD gate and the frame-class narrowing before merge.
